reviews.checked_passages: Logic planning: §§2.1–2.4, machine examples, primitive recursion and coding; §2.7, universal/halting argument; §§4.3–4.5, Q representation, undecidability and diagonal lemma; §4.7, conditional second incompleteness. Model equivalence §2.6 and c.e./Rice chapters located but not fully audited.  New entry audit: §1.2, 9, partial-function graphs; §§2.3–2.4, 20–30, initial functions, primitive recursion, bounded operations, numerical coding and history recursion; §2.5, 33–35, strict partial operations and sequential minimization; §4.3, 90–91, arithmetic axioms and induction. Coverage comparison 2026-10-19: §2.5, 31–32, diagonal separation from primitive recursion; §2.7, 42–43, normal form and universality; §3.1, 57–58, parameter theorem; selected definitions and argument excerpts in §§3.2–3.4, 59–75, enumerable sets, reductions, Rice and program fixed points. These are planning checks, not full machine/compiler proof audits.  Batch 2026-10-19: §2.6, 35–41, primitive-recursive state transitions and finite histories; §2.5, 31–32, primitive-recursive diagonal separation; §2.7, 42–45, full universality and halting arguments; §§3.1–3.2, 57–65, parameter theorem and enumerable-set equivalences/closure; §4.4, 103–104, Lemmas 4.4.7–4.4.8, theorem enumeration and two-sided proof search. Representability source audit 2026-10-19: full selected §4.3, 90–100, including the total-function definition, beta/primitive-recursion simulation, basis/composition, finite numeral cuts and regular minimization; p. 98 displayed minimization formula checked against the corrected Open Logic construction. Self-reference audit 2026-10-20: §4.5, 107–109, full fixed-point proof and numeral/code distinction; the proof uses strong numeralwise representation of the total diagonal function. Incompleteness/provability audit 2026-10-20: §§4.4–4.7, 103–115, actual proof enumeration and two-sided search, essential undecidability, Gödel consistency and omega-consistency arguments, the Rosser construction (whose proof is assigned as an exercise), and the stated derivability-condition assumptions.
reviews.outcome: [AVIGAD-CI-01](source-errors/findings/AVIGAD-CI-01.json), [02](source-errors/findings/AVIGAD-CI-02.json). Concrete derivability conditions are accepted rather than fully proved in the inspected argument; this is an explicit coverage limit. CRT is invoked without its proof.  No new serious defect found in these adopted entry passages. The entry uses explicit square-pair list codes and proves its own bounds, replacing the prime-code convention; minimization requires all earlier tests to be defined.  The new entries adopt arithmetic macro steps and explicitly prove paired-program compilation, bounded evaluation and both machine simulations; they make no tape-runtime claim. The regular-minimization bound must be the proposed output, as recorded in AVIGAD-CI-01. The adopted function theorem concerns total computable functions; no claim about divergent inputs is imported. The corpus supplies the finite remainder/CRT argument and explicit numeral reasoning rather than treating omitted proofs as checked.  No serious defect found in the selected fixed-point proof; the corpus supplies the total invalid-code convention and uses its own coded substitution. No additional serious defect found in the selected incompleteness arguments. AVIGAD-CI-02 remains a necessary consistency repair. Section 4.7, p. 113, explicitly assumes rather than proves the concrete PA derivability conditions; the corpus distinguishes a numeralwise-certified proof transformation from a uniform arithmetic theorem.
